net.lemnik.eodsql

Class NullDataSetCache<T>

  • java.lang.Object
    • net.lemnik.eodsql.NullDataSetCache<T>
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    DataSetCache<T>

    public class NullDataSetCache<T>
extends Object
implements DataSetCache<T>
    An implementation of DataSetCache that does not cache rows. This implementation can be used for very large DataSets, but it forces every call to "get()" to re-fetch the row (and therefore reconstruct the Object).
    Author:
    Jason Morris

      • init

        public void init(DataSet<T> dataSet)
        Description copied from interface: DataSetCache
        Initialize this DataSetCache, which will be used to cache rows for the DataSet specified here. There is generally no reason to store the parent DataSet, but it is given anyway.

        init in interface DataSetCache<T>
        Parameters:

      • isCached

        public boolean isCached(int row)
        Description copied from interface: DataSetCache

        A quick check to see if the specified row is currently cached. This method does not guarentee that getObject will return a non-null value, but it suggests that it probably won't. If this method returns false however, it is assumed that getObject will return a null value, and that the object should be re-fetched from the database.

        The row passed into this method will never be negative, but any other value is possible. The cache is expected to be zero-based.

        Specified by:
        isCached in interface DataSetCache<T>
        Parameters:
        row - the row number to check
        Returns:
        true if the object is probably cached

      • getObject

        public T getObject(int row)
        Description copied from interface: DataSetCache
        Returns the object at the specified row. If the row is not found in the cache, this method may return null. If the return-value from this method is null, the row will be fetched from the database.
        Specified by:
        getObject in interface DataSetCache<T>
        Parameters:
        row - the row to look for
        Returns:
        the value cached in the row
        See Also:
        DataSetCache.isCached(int)

      • setObject

        public void setObject(int row,
                      T object)
        Description copied from interface: DataSetCache
        Sets the value of a row in this cache. This is generally called directly after a call to DataSetCache.isCached(int) or DataSetCache.getObject(int) to set the value of the specified row. The object value given here will never be null.
        Specified by:
        setObject in interface DataSetCache<T>
        Parameters:
        row - the row index
        object - the value of the row

      • destroy

        public void destroy()
        Description copied from interface: DataSetCache
        Free's up any resources used by this DataSetCache. This method should also make a best effort to flag any used resources for garbage-colletion. No method in this DataSetCache will be used after this method is called.
        Specified by:
